quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until the signal lights stop flashing.
Watch for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Even after a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not go forward until all gates are lifted and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow-moving vehicle.
Road construction or maintenance area.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: Your driver license can be revoked or suspended for:

options.text: Getting 12 or more points on your driving record from traffic violations.
Changing your driver license illegally.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A license can be revoked or suspended for several reasons. These include illegally changing your driver license or getting 12 or more points in 12 months. Drivers under 18 may lose their license if they get 6 points in 12 months.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses grip on water on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at the same speed to get better grip.
Brake hard to stop your vehicle from sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: In heavy rain, even at 30 mph, your tires may lose contact with the road and ride on a layer of water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the other driver passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: To avoid being blinded at night, do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.

questions.question: You should not enter an intersection if you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Even if the light is green, do not enter an intersection unless you can cross it completely before the light turns red. Blocking the intersection can result in a ticket.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Give the right-of-way to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to places where bicycles may be crossing.

questions.question: How do you see vehicles in your blind spots?

options.text: Check the inside rearview mirror.
Check the outside rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: By definition, blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. To check your blind spots, look over your shoulders.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
They all have air brakes that let them stop quickly.
They are easier to steer than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more distance to stop than other vehicles traveling at the same speed. A passenger vehicle at 55 mph can stop in about 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: When it is hard to see because of darkness or bad weather, increase the distance between you and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to dangers you might not see coming.

questions.question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?

options.text: In an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles
Wherever signs and road markings allow passing
On a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever signs and road markings allow passing
questions.explanation: Never pass in intersections or at other crossing points like parking lot entrances and alleys. If a curve or hill blocks your view, stay in your lane and assume an oncoming vehicle is nearby. Only pass where signs and markings allow it, and only if you have enough safe space.

questions.question: When changing lanes, how can you check your blind spot?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all blind spots in your vehicle. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to see these hidden areas.

questions.question: Why should you not use high beam headlights in fog or mist?

options.text: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
Oncoming vehicles might not see you.
Vehicles behind you may follow too closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will reflect back into your eyes.
questions.explanation: In fog or mist, high beam headlights reflect back toward you and reduce visibility instead of improving it.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, which lane should you start from?

options.text: Any lane, as long as it is safe
The lane closest to the left curb
The center lane of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, start the turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: What information do blue traffic signs provide?

options.text: Motorist services
Construction and maintenance
Distances to specific locations

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorist services
questions.explanation: Blue signs tell drivers about services available nearby, such as rest areas, food, gas, or hospitals.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield to you.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must always yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the road edge, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down, check traffic, then gradually return to the road
Turn back onto the road immediately
Stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, check traffic, then gradually return to the road
questions.explanation: Do not try to turn back onto the road right away. Instead, reduce speed, check for traffic, and gradually steer back onto the road when it is safe.

questions.question: When passing, when do you have enough space to return to your lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to return
When you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you
When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror
questions.explanation: It is safe to return to your lane when you can see both headlights of the car you passed in your rearview mirror. This means there is enough distance between your vehicles.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to your lane mean?

options.text: You cannot pass in this area
You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present
You can only make right turns in this area

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass other vehicles on the left if no oncoming traffic is present
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means passing is allowed from that side of the road if it is safe.

questions.question: You are in a minor collision with no injuries and little damage. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible
Do not move your vehicle for any reason

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible
questions.explanation: After a collision with no injuries, move your vehicle out of traffic if you can do so safely.

questions.question: What can you do at a broken white centerline?

options.text: You must stay in your lane.
You can cross to change lanes.
You can change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can cross to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines mean lanes go the same direction. A broken white line means you can pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and go carefully.
Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, look for cross traffic, and proceed with caution.

questions.question: Which lane should you use to turn left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane closest to the center of the street.
The lane closest to the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: To turn left, use the lane closest to the direction you want to turn. On a one-way street turning left, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
Merge right.
Turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for traffic merging from the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane from the right.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a crash.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn to prevent crashes. Do not use it to tell someone to drive faster or get out of your way.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a large truck?

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your car.
Do not drive beside it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on each side. Avoid driving next to them for extended periods.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign shows a crosswalk. Be alert and let pedestrians cross safely.

questions.question: What should you do in a construction zone?

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Follow the vehicle ahead more closely.
Pass through carefully and do not look at unusual things.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass through carefully and do not look at unusual things.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at out-of-the-ordinary things. This causes traffic jams.

questions.question: What must you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, be aware, and proceed with caution. Watch for other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: When is it safe to move back into the right lane after passing?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, move back into the right lane when you can see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.
